newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall sharply in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall sharply in early trading.

text.p: Wall Street stocks plunged in early morning trading Wednesday, pressured by reports and rumours that called into question the recent strength of blue chips and technology stocks, including powerhouse IBM Corp.
Shortly after the 9.30 a.m. EST opening, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 91.11 points at 6,382.14 and the technology-laced Nasdaq Composite index was off 15.92 at 1,296.63.
Analysts said the market was rocked by worries that Japanese investors might reduce their holdings of U.S. stocks and bonds.

Also rattling the stock market, which on Monday bounced back nicely from last Friday's sell-off, were rumours that International Business Machines Corp. -- a pacesetter among blue-chip stocks -- was about to issue a profit warning.

There were also concerns about a column in the Wall Street Journal questioning whether Japanese institutions were losing their appetite for U.S. Treasuries, which sent the bond market down sharply at its opening.
"It looks like a very rough morning," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Regarding the Wall Street Journal report, which appeared in its Heard on the Street column, Wachtel said, "We've seen these stories time and time again, but because this one comes from (Goldman Sachs International Vice Chairman Robert) Hormats, it carries some weight."
In the U.S. Treasuries market, the benchmark 30-year bond was off more than a full point, boosting its yield to 6.58 percent from 6.49 percent Tuesday.
An IBM spokesman told Reuters the company had no comment on the profit-warning rumours. However, he said IBM had no plans to issue a press release on Wednesday.
